concerns.text: Phase 6 (T050-T053) introduces a 'Computational Universe' explorer and 'Simple Programs' approach (Wolfram-style cellular automata) that is entirely absent from spec.md and plan.md. The spec explicitly restricts the approach to a Random Forest regressor with ILR transformation (FR-004, FR-006). This task set constitutes unauthorized scope creep and a semantic weakening of the defined research methodology, violating the constraint that tasks must not silently relax or alter the spec's core approach.

Task T009a includes a hard halt condition: 'If no data is retrieved, raise RuntimeError...'. However, the spec.md Assumptions section explicitly states: 'The Materials Project and NIST Materials Data Repository APIs are publicly accessible without authentication'. The task's implementation logic (requiring an API key or failing if data is missing due to auth) contradicts the spec's assumption of keyless/public access, effectively weakening the FR-001 requirement to work with public data by introducing an unmandated authentication barrier.

Task T028 computes VIF on 'ILR-transformed features' and logs raw VIF only as a 'diagnostic note'. This contradicts spec.md FR-007 which mandates: 'System MUST compute variance inflation factors (VIF) for raw predictors as a diagnostic and flag any with VIF >5'. While the plan.md notes that raw VIF is 'infinite', the task description fails to implement the explicit requirement to compute and flag raw predictors, instead substituting a different metric (ILR VIF) as the primary pass/fail check without a documented waiver or spec amendment.

Tasks T020, T021, and T024 are marked as incomplete (`[ ]`) in the tasks document. These tasks are the core deliverables for FR-004 (ILR + CV), FR-005 (80/20 split + test MAE), and SC-002 (Model accuracy). A task list that omits the implementation of mandatory functional requirements (FR-004, FR-005) constitutes a failure to preserve the spec's constraints, as the deliverable described by the task list falls short of the spec's demands.
